title: Dedicated autoscaler: add cooldown + dampening + min-step guardrails to reduce oscillation (predictive mode)
author: Keiko Yamamoto
description: Problem: During pilot with predictive inputs enabled (see SUP-28479 + incident follow-ups), we observed replica count oscillation caused by noisy/stale forecast deltas and small target changes around the steady-state. This manifested as jittery queue depth and p95 latency spikes, even when we stayed within min/max bounds (PR #48218). This PR adds three guardrails to the Dedicated autoscaler decision loop: (1) per-direction cooldowns to prevent back-to-back flips (scale-up immediately followed by scale-down), (2) dampening / smoothing of predictive desired replicas using an EWMA + a limited lookback window, and (3) minimum step sizing + hysteresis around the current capacity so we don’t chase 1-replica fluctuations. These changes apply only when predictive mode is active OR when the autoscaler classifies the input signal as noisy (high variance in desired over a short window). Reactive saturation/queue depth overrides remain authoritative, and all results are still clamped to customer bounds. Summary of behavior: - Compute raw_desired from reactive + predictive arbitration (existing logic). - Clamp to bounds => bounded_desired_raw. - Apply dampening to bounded_desired_raw to produce dampened_desired (EWMA with alpha=0.35 by default; configurable per deployment in the policy, defaulted off unless predictive enabled). - Apply hysteresis: require |dampened_desired - current| >= min_step_replicas OR min_percent_change before taking action. - Apply per-direction cooldowns: if last_scale_event was < cooldown_{up,down}, hold desired at current (unless reactive override requires immediate scale-up for safety; scale-up bypasses cooldown when queue_depth/latency breach thresholds). - Emit structured reason codes + metrics for each hold/action for auditability and debugging. Defaults were chosen to preserve existing behavior for deployments without predictive enabled (no cooldown/dampening applied) and to make predictive mode safer out of the box. Related: - PR #48227 (predictive provider + fallback) - PR #48218 (hard min/max enforcement) - PR #48241 (desired vs bounded metrics) - Hotfix PR #48321 (prevent scale-to-zero when predictor returns null) Testing: - Unit tests for cooldown boundary conditions and hysteresis thresholds - Property-style tests with randomized desired sequences to ensure no oscillation under small noise - Simulation replay updates (lightweight) to validate reduced event rate without increased underprovisioning under standard ramp traces
commits: autoscaler: add EWMA dampening for predictive desired replicas
metrics: emit hold_reason and dampening deltas
tests: add oscillation regression suite w/ noisy predictor sequences
docs: update internal autoscaler tuning notes for pilot ops
conversation: Vanessa Ortiz (review): Cooldown semantics look good, but I’m worried about blocking legitimate scale-down after an emergency scale-up. Can we make scale-up bypass cooldown when reactive override fires, but keep scale-down cooled? Also please confirm we still always respect min/max. Keiko Yamamoto (author): Updated. Scale-up cooldown is bypassed when reactive_override=true (queue depth / saturation breach), but scale-down still obeys cooldown_down unless bounded_desired == min and reactive is green. Bounds clamp happens before dampening and again after rounding. Added tests for clamp order and a docstring. Jordan Lee (review): Where does alpha live? If this becomes a policy field, we need to ensure validation ranges and sane defaults. Also, avoid per-request state; this should be per-deployment keyed with TTL. Keiko Yamamoto: Alpha is a constant default (0.35) with optional override read from policy cache (0.05..0.9). State is per deployment_id in the autoscaler process with eviction after 2h of inactivity; no request path impact. Added guardrails when predictor staleness > 15m => disable dampening and fall back to reactive-only desired (existing fallback). Rafael Mendes (review): Please add explicit metrics for “hold due to cooldown” vs “hold due to hysteresis” so on-call can reason about why it’s not scaling. Also ensure we don’t hide an unmet-min condition behind cooldown. Keiko Yamamoto: Added metrics: dedicated_autoscaler_hold_total{reason=...}, dedicated_autoscaler_cooldown_active{direction=...}, and dedicated_autoscaler_dampening_delta. Unmet-min bypasses all holds (we keep requesting min) and we emit hold_reason=none with state=degraded elsewhere. Samantha Roy (review): Any risk this increases time-to-react during ramps? We should verify with the replay runner. Keiko Yamamoto: Ran replay on ramp_with_spikes fixture: scale event count -41%, p95 queue depth +2.3% at peak but stayed below alert threshold; time-to-recover unchanged. Notes added to README. CI: Initial run failed on gofmt in stabilizer.go; fixed in follow-up commit. Final checks green (unit/integration/sim). Approvals: Vanessa ✅, Rafael ✅, Jordan ✅. Merged via squash.
release_notes: Dedicated autoscaler: added cooldowns, dampening, and minimum-step sizing to reduce oscillation when predictive scaling inputs are noisy; includes new hold-reason metrics for observability. No behavior change unless predictive mode is enabled (or policy explicitly opts into stabilization).
